notebook: Bulbasaur (Grass/Poison) is super-effective against Rock-type gym leaders (e.g., Brock). Use Bulbasaur as lead for the first gym.
When facing a Hiker trainer (Rock/Ground), set lead to a Water-type Pokémon (e.g., Psyduck) for super-effective advantage and gain +2 levels to that lead.
Catching a Water-type early (e.g., Staryu) provides strong coverage against Fire trainers and serves as a backup lead for Water-type gyms.
Team Rocket Grunt trainers use Poison‑type Pokemon; a Psychic or Ground lead (e.g., Alakazam or Diglett) has super‑effective advantage, while Grass leads are weak to Poison.
Firebreather trainer uses Fire-type Pokemon; a Water-type lead (e.g., Tentacool) wins and grants +2 levels.
Misty (Water) gym is weak to Grass (Ivysaur) or Electric leads; set lead to Ivysaur before battling.
Miracle Seed held item boosts Grass move damage; equip on any Grass-type lead (e.g., Bulbasaur) before battles where Grass is super-effective.
Trainer nodes (e.g., Ace Trainer, Gentleman) grant +2 levels to the lead Pokémon; always take them before a gym if the lead is healthy.
Bug Catcher trainers use Bug-type Pokemon; a Grass-type lead (e.g., Bulbasaur) is super-effective and grants +2 levels.
At move tutor, teach Bulbasaur ENERGY BALL (Grass) to replace Magical Leaf, maximizing Grass damage with Miracle Seed for the upcoming Water-type gym.
Take the wild battle at layer 1 before catching; it gives +1 level to the lead (Bulbasaur) and keeps the catch node available on layer 2, ensuring a stronger lead for early trainers.
Hiker trainers (Rock/Ground) can be defeated by a Fighting-type lead (e.g., Mankey) OR a Water-type lead (e.g., Seel) for +2 levels.
Sacred Ash fully restores HP and revives fainted Pokémon. Use it before a gym if your lead (e.g., Bulbasaur) is fainted to ensure you have a viable counter.
Eviolite on a non‑final stage Pokemon (e.g., Drowzee) gives +50% DEF/Sp.DEF and is valuable before early gyms; take it when available.
Set lead before each battle (free action) to ensure the Pokemon with a type advantage leads, greatly increasing win chances.
If your lead Pokémon is fainted before a gym, immediately set lead to a healthy team member and go to the next Pokécenter to heal before the gym battle.
If any team members are fainted before a gym, go to the Pokécenter first to revive them, ensuring a viable lead for the gym battle.
Map 3 (after 3 badges) gym is Grass-type; set a Poison-type lead (e.g., Weezing) for super-effective advantage.
Never enter a gym with any team member below 30% HP; use the Pokécenter at layer 7 before the final gym to fully heal.
map 1 layer 3 Bug Catcher trainer uses Bug-type Pokemon; a Grass lead (Bulbasaur) wins and grants +2 levels.
map 0 layer2 trainer Bug Catcher is weak to Grass lead; set Bulbasaur as lead to gain +2 levels.
Heal at Pokecenter before the first gym to ensure all Pokemon are at full HP; entering a gym with low HP leads to unnecessary fainting and loss of badges.
Fisherman trainer (water) is weak to Grass leads (e.g., Ivysaur); using a Grass lead yields super-effective advantage and +2 levels. Use this trainer to boost Grass lead before Electric gym.
Hiker trainers use Rock/Ground Pokemon; a Fighting-type lead (e.g., Mankey) is super-effective against Rock and safe vs Ground, giving +2 levels.
If team has only one healthy Pokemon, prioritize the trade node to obtain a stronger lead before facing a trainer or gym.
Officer trainer (Fire-type Pokemon) is best countered by a Water-type lead (e.g., Tentacool or Poliwag) for super-effective advantage and +2 levels.
Choosing the Girl starter gives Bulbasaur (Grass/Poison). Set Bulbasaur as lead immediately; its Grass moves are super-effective against the first Rock-type gym (Brock).
Shell Bell passive item heals 15% of damage dealt; equip on lead (e.g., Bulbasaur) for extra survivability in trainer battles and gym.
Start with Bulbasaur (Grass/Poison) as starter; leads give super-effective advantage vs early Rock-type trainers and gyms (e.g., Brock).
Hiker trainers (Rock/Ground) are best countered by Water or Fighting-type leads for +2 levels; ensure such a lead before facing them.
At move tutor nodes, teach Bulbasaur ENERGY BALL (Grass) to replace Magical Leaf for stronger damage, especially before Water-type gyms.
When presented with item choices before the first gym, choose Expert Belt for the lead Pokémon if its type is super-effective against the gym leader, to double damage on super-effective hits.
Use Rare Candy on the lead Water-type (Seel) before the Water-type gym (Misty) to raise it to level 15, ensuring a strong counter if needed, but primarily set Bulbasaur as lead for the gym.
Ace Trainer nodes grant +2 levels; set lead to Grass-type (Ivysaur) before taking them to boost for the upcoming Water gym.
Expert Belt should be equipped on the Pokémon that will have a super‑effective move against the upcoming gym leader; keep it in the bag until that lead is known, then equip before the gym battle.
Catch Diglett early for Ground coverage; useful against Fire gym (Blaine) and Poison gym (Koga).
Teach Earthquake (Ground) to Diglett before the Electric-type gym; Diglett as lead will have a strong super-effective move against the gym leader.
If you have a Water-type lead, taking the Fire trainer (Officer) for +2 levels is beneficial before the first gym; otherwise avoid the Fire trainer with a Grass lead.
Expert Belt gives +100% damage on super-effective hits; equip on the lead before a gym where its type is super-effective for maximum damage.
Equip Leftovers on the lead Pokémon before a gym; its passive HP recovery helps keep the lead alive through the battle.
runs.plan: n0_1: Choose Girl starter (Bulbasaur). Immediately set lead to Bulbasaur (free). Next aim: locate Pokécenter on layer 1 to fully heal before first gym. Plan to catch a Water-type (e.g., Squirtle) on layer 2 for backup, then head toward the first gym (Brock) with Bulbasaur as lead.
